episodes.title: Is Yoga a Religion?
episodes.description: Use yoga to explore the difficulties and real-world consequences of defining religion.

episodes.title: How Many Religions Are There?
episodes.description: Question how the familiar world-religions category was constructed and which communities it excludes.

episodes.title: What’s the Difference Between Cults and Religion?
episodes.description: Explore why scholars question the apparent boundary between cults and religions.

episodes.title: What’s the Difference Between Religion and Magic?
episodes.description: Trace magical practices and the ways contemporary communities reclaim labels historically used against them.

episodes.title: The Infinite Stories of Hinduism
episodes.description: Investigate Hindu identity, karma, and the tradition's many overlapping stories.

episodes.title: Life, the Universe, and the Buddha
episodes.description: Explore Buddhist approaches to suffering through foundational teachings and paths toward enlightenment.

episodes.title: Can a River Be A Person? | Indigenous Traditions
episodes.description: Examine place, ancestry, kinship, and spirits in Indigenous traditions and their challenge to Western assumptions.

episodes.title: What Does it Mean to Be Jewish
episodes.description: Explore the intertwined religious, cultural, national, and communal meanings of Jewish identity.

episodes.title: Sacrifice, Redemption, and Miracles: The Story of Christianity
episodes.description: Investigate Christianity's many traditions, their shared features, and their important differences.

episodes.title: The History and Practice of Islam on Earth and Beyond
episodes.description: Explore Islamic beliefs, practices, history, and adaptations from early astronomy to space travel.

episodes.title: Religions of the African Diaspora
episodes.description: Follow African religious traditions and their transformation under forced migration and diaspora.

episodes.title: China | Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism
episodes.description: Explore Confucian and Daoist traditions and the fluidity of religious practice in China.

episodes.title: Is Atheism a Religion?
episodes.description: Compare diverse forms of nonbelief and consider whether atheism fits the category of religion.

episodes.title: How Do Religious Texts Work?
episodes.description: Investigate how communities interpret, debate, honor, and use sacred writings.

episodes.title: What Does Ritual Have to Do with Religion?
episodes.description: Explore how rituals organize time, transform identity, and connect people within and beyond religion.

episodes.title: Who Speaks for a Religion?
episodes.description: Examine the sources of religious leadership and how communities can contest that authority.

episodes.title: Death and Afterlife Across Religions
episodes.description: Compare beliefs about life after death and trace changing ideas of heaven and hell.

episodes.title: Religion, Spirituality, and the Supernatural
episodes.description: Explore paranormal and supernatural beliefs across religious traditions and spiritual identities.

episodes.title: Are Science and Religion Compatible?
episodes.description: Look beyond famous disputes to investigate different relationships between scientific and religious practice.

episodes.title: What Do Sex and Gender Have to Do with Religion?
episodes.description: Explore how communities shape changing understandings of gender, sexuality, and sex.

episodes.title: What Does Race Have to Do with Religion?
episodes.description: Investigate connections between racial categories, colonial religion, boarding schools, and continuing racism.

episodes.title: Visions of the End of the World
episodes.description: Compare apocalyptic predictions and the present-day concerns they often express.

episodes.title: What Does Religious Freedom Mean?
episodes.description: Explore competing interpretations and practical limits of constitutional protections for religious freedom.

episodes.title: Religions and Pop Culture
episodes.description: Investigate the two-way relationship between religious ideas and popular culture.
